page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on KVM hypervisor architecture. The instance features 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores operating at 2.7 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 64 GB of system RAM, allocating 4 GB of memory per core. The underlying processor includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, along with hardware flag support for AVX-512, VNNI, AES, and SHA vector instructions.

The server lacks integrated local NVMe or SSD storage and relies entirely on external network-attached volumes. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps. For compute and memory benchmarks, the ecs.g7t.4xlarge falls into average performance brackets across standardized testing suites. Measured memory performance includes an uncached read bandwidth of 97.84 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 57.96 GB/sec. Synthetic CPU tests yield a multi-core stress-ng score of 15531.53 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9721.0.

Application-specific workloads show balanced performance profiles. Redis SET operations reach 15.69 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 20.98 GB/sec. Small language model inference tests on a 7B parameter model achieved 32.29 tokens per second for prompt processing and 11.58 tokens per second for text generation. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a practical design for containerized application servers, intermediate database engines, web applications, and software compilation tasks where specialized GPU acceleration or dedicated local storage is not required.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor featuring 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 64 GB of memory. It provides a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 48 MB L3 cache and instruction set support for AVX-512 and AES vector extensions. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor with 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, though it lacks direct local storage. Synthetic benchmarks position its processing capability and memory bandwidth within average performance tiers, highlighted by an uncached read memory speed of 97.84 GB/sec and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9721.0. Real-world benchmark performance demonstrates high Redis SET throughput at 15.69 million operations per second and static web serving speeds of 20.98 GB/sec. This configuration is suitable for mid-tier web applications, software compilation, memory-cached key-value stores, and general application workloads requiring balanced system resources.
